predecessors.name: Sasanian Empire
predecessors.text: Bahram VI's kingdom of 590: Ctesiphon and Mesopotamia, the northern commands of Media, and Khorasan

successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: returned to Khosrow II, restored with Byzantine help

ledger.x: Summer 590: Bahram Chobin takes Ctesiphon and proclaims himself king of kings.
591: Khosrow II, restored with Byzantine help, retakes Mesopotamia and Ctesiphon from Bahram.
August 591: Bahram loses Khorasan after Blarathon.
August 591: Bahram is defeated at Blarathon and flees east to the Turks; his kingdom ends.

wars.name: Sasanian civil war of 589-591
wars.outcome: Khosrow II, restored by Emperor Maurice's army, defeated Bahram at Blarathon in August 591; Maurice received much of Sasanian Armenia and western Georgia and the abolition of tribute.

wars.name: Battle of Blarathon
wars.outcome: Khosrow II's combined Byzantine and Persian army overran Bahram's camp; Bahram fled east to the Turks.

certainty.note: A usurper's kingdom held by an army: no frontier is described; Mesopotamia fell to Khosrow within 591.
